body:
## What to build

Keep contextual share columns double when a caller partially collects a SQLite Margin result and every share in the requested nonempty prefix is missing. A row limit must not change a package-created share's declared type.

## Reproduction and observed behavior

Confirmed on unmodified [6a5f611](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/commit/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892), installed in an isolated library and exercised without testthat. R 4.6.1, dplyr 1.2.1, dbplyr 2.6.0, DBI 1.3.0, RSQLite 3.53.3.

1. Open an in-memory SQLite connection and copy a tibble with character `g = c("a", "b")` and double `v = c(NA_real_, 1)`.
2. Call `summarize_with_margins()` with `total = sum(v, na.rm = TRUE)`, `share = share_of_total(total)`, `.grouping = rollup(g)`, `.sort = "last"`, and `.check_share_source = FALSE`.
3. Compare full direct collection, direct `collect(n = 1)`, and `collect(compute(query), n = 1)`.

Observed share columns:

| Retrieval | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| Full direct collection | double `c(NA_real_, 1, 1)` | correct |
| Direct one-row prefix | double `NA_real_` | logical `NA` |
| One-row prefix after compute | double `NA_real_` | correct |

The source-eligibility opt-out is the documented way to use a known numeric source on SQLite's Converting dialect. It does not waive output type guarantees.

An independent investigator reproduced the mismatch without missing input values: fixed partitions `c("A", "A", "B")`, grouping values `c("x", "y", "z")`, and measures `c(2, -2, 3)`. The first partition's zero denominator creates missing shares. Full and materialized partial retrieval remain double, while direct one-row retrieval becomes logical. Default and typed-missing labels both reproduce it; a nonmissing prefix remains double and the source is unchanged. The larger workflow also reproduces the same cause for Parent shares and mean-source Total shares.

## Contract, diagnosis, and history

The [share reference](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892/R/share.R) promises that a share is always a double and that missing numerators or zero/missing denominators produce a missing double. [ADR 0031](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892/design/adr/0031-preserve-sqlite-typed-dimensions-under-margin-order.md) retains direct finite collection.

[The dedicated collection method](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892/R/sqlite-typed-order.R), `collect.marginplyr_sqlite_typed_result()`, restores declared types only when the entire result has zero rows. RSQLite infers logical for an all-NULL column in a nonempty prefix; that case bypasses the restoration even though the share's double declaration is already available.

An ordinary dbplyr all-NULL expression also exhibits driver inference. That control limits the claim: repair the types marginplyr explicitly promises, not all ordinary aggregate types or arbitrary downstream transformations.

#653 / #658 repaired zero-row declared types, and #654 / #659 repaired row-limit validation and unintended warnings. Neither covers this nonempty, finite, all-NULL intersection. The same dependencies reproduce it before both fixes at `d4ea5f09d5698a6a89b68ecfd62ad450a4089bba` and before #640 at `ad851dbefe99cf1cf6987dc5f0716f6a13d3873b`. This is a remaining boundary defect, not an established new regression from #651–#655.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Direct finite collection of an all-missing share prefix returns a double column containing `NA_real_`, with the requested row count and correct values.
- [ ] Cover Parent and Total shares, sum and mean sources, missing and zero denominators, and fixed partitions. Include direct and across-generated shares where supported.
- [ ] Verify zero-row, nonempty all-missing, mixed/nonmissing prefixes, and unlimited collection; preserve correct full and materialized collection and both Margin-order choices.
- [ ] Preserve column names/order, other declared output types, public-only columns, and existing row-limit validation and warning behavior from #654.
- [ ] Do not impose new R-type guarantees on ordinary aggregates or arbitrary downstream dplyr results. Add public-API regression tests with independent values and driver controls, and run the required package checks.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately). Registering expansion identifiers is a separate type-declaration issue and is not required to fix this already-declared share type.

title: Keep missing contextual shares double during finite SQLite collection
